eligibility.evidence: Sections 2-3, p.21951-21952: the only task is the Oxford Utilitarianism Scale (9 agree/disagree statements, expanded to 99 by GPT-4 generation), a self-report moral-attitude questionnaire compared with lay-population means. No experimental manipulation of dilemmas, so it falls under attitude questionnaires; borderline because the OUS is a validated cognitive-science instrument on moral dilemmas.

A.title: The Greatest Good Benchmark: Measuring LLMs' Alignment with Utilitarian Moral Dilemmas

G.notes: Excluded as an attitude questionnaire; if the panel treats the OUS as a moral-judgement paradigm it would be YES (15 models, 2 OUS subscales, human lay-population means from Kahane et al. 2018, prompt-wording and option-order variants, temperature 0 and 0.5, 10 repeats). Referee would ask whether the OUS counts as a moral dilemma task.
